title: Ensure linear history is required
description: A linear history keeps the record of what shipped simple to read and to bisect. Merge commits let a branch's history be reshaped in ways that are hard to audit after the fact. Without a "Limit merge types" policy, Azure Repos offers every merge type, including the two that create merge commits.
remediation: Project settings -> Repositories -> <repository> -> Policies -> Branch Policies -> <default branch>: set "Limit merge types" to On and allow only Squash merge and/or Rebase and fast-forward; leave Basic merge (no fast-forward) and Rebase with merge commit (semi-linear) off — both create merge commits. Set it on the project-wide policy at Project settings -> Repositories -> All Repositories -> Policies -> Branch Policies to cover every repository. If your workflow requires merge commits, edit nonLinearMergeStrategies in azure-devops-bench's config (no-ff is Basic merge, rebase-no-ff the semi-linear merge).
fixSummary: Allow only squash or rebase merges at Project settings -> Repositories -> <repo> -> Policies.
